name: Navigation Bar (Responsive) with Mobile Menu
description: A responsive top bar for a site or app: a skip link, the logo, links with disclosure dropdowns, and the actions, plus a menu in a native dialog below 1024 px. It sticks with CSS alone, keeps focused elements clear of itself with scroll-padding, and stays below modals.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The bar is a sticky bar: an open dropdown list sits above the page, and a modal dialog covers the bar.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a site's or app's top bar: a skip link, the logo, the main links with disclosure dropdowns, and the actions, plus a menu in a native dialog below 1024 px. The bar sticks with position: sticky, and scroll-padding-top keeps focused elements clear of it. Dropdowns are disclosures, never ARIA menus: a button that shows a list of links, closed by Escape, a click outside, or focus leaving the navigation. Build on the project's header or navigation component when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A <header> that starts with a skip link, a labelled <nav> with the links, and aria-current="page" on the current one
Sticky with CSS alone, and scroll-padding-top at the bar's height, so focused elements and link targets stay clear of it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11)
Disclosure dropdowns: a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, a hidden list while closed, Escape back to the button, and closing when focus leaves or on a click outside
Below 1024 px, a menu in a native dialog that makes the page inert, with a visible Close button and accordion sections for groups
An app variant with an account menu that signs out with a button, and a notifications button whose name has the count
Optional: a transparent bar over a hero that turns solid once the page scrolls, switched by an IntersectionObserver
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the router, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a header or navigation component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Choose what the task needs: the marketing or the app variant (componentSpec.variants), dropdowns, the transparent state. Leave out the rest.
3. Build the structure (componentSpec.anatomy): the header, the skip link, the logo, the labelled nav, and the actions.
4. Make the bar sticky, and set scroll-padding-top to its height (frameworkPatterns.skipLink).
6. Below 1024 px, add the Menu button and the menu in a native dialog (implementationDetails.mobileMenu).
7. For the app variant, add the account menu and the notifications button (implementationDetails.appActions).
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and 200% zoom, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Give every page the same way to its main sections, one that works with a keyboard, a pointer, a touch screen, and a screen reader, and never covers what has focus.

anatomy.hierarchy: header (banner) → skip link | logo link | nav "Main" → list of links and dropdown buttons, each button followed by its list | actions (a call to action, or the account menu and notifications) | Menu button (below 1024 px) → dialog "Main menu" with its own copy of the links and actions

slotNotes.header: The bar is the page's <header>, its banner landmark. It starts with the skip link, then the logo, a link to the home page named with the site's name (the logo image's alt text), then a <nav> with the site's links, labelled "Main", then the actions.
slotNotes.currentLink: The current page's link has aria-current="page" and looks different by more than color, such as an underline.
slotNotes.unavailableLink: Leave out links the person can't use. One that has to show as unavailable for now is an <a> without href, with role="link", tabindex="0", and aria-disabled="true", so it's still found and does nothing; say why next to it.
slotNotes.newTab: A link that opens a new tab says so in its text, visible or visually hidden.
slotNotes.dropdownButton: An item with children is a button that shows or hides its list of links, with aria-expanded and aria-controls. It has no aria-haspopup and no role="menu": those announce an app menu with arrow-key behavior, and these are links.
slotNotes.linkWithChildren: An item with its own page and children needs two controls: the link, and a separate button that shows the list, named after it ("More Products pages").
slotNotes.skipLink: The skip link is the first focusable element: "Skip to content", shown while it has focus, going to <main id="main" tabindex="-1"> (WCAG 2.4.1).

openDropdown.description: The id of the open dropdown list, or empty when none is open; mirrored in aria-expanded on its button.

menuOpen.description: Whether the menu dialog is open, below 1024 px.

activeLink.description: The link for the current page, which gets aria-current="page".
activeLink.determination: Compare the current route with the links' targets

scrolled.description: Optional: whether the page has scrolled past the top, for the transparent state or a shadow.
scrolled.determination: An IntersectionObserver on a small element at the top of the page

interactions.accessibilityNotes: A click, Enter, or Space toggles the list; focus stays on the button.
Escape closes the open list and puts focus back on its button.
A focusout whose relatedTarget is outside the navigation closes the list. A null relatedTarget is left to the click handler, since macOS Safari doesn't focus a clicked link.
Focus stays where the click put it.
showModal() puts focus on the dialog's first control and makes the rest of the page inert.
Close, Escape, a click on the backdrop, and a followed link close it; the browser returns focus to the Menu button.

React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events. Focus on what hides moves to what stays: widening with the menu open, or with focus on the Menu button, moves focus to a link in the bar; narrowing with focus on the bar's links moves it to the Menu button; focus anywhere else stays. Chromium drops focus from a hidden element before the listener runs, so remember the last focused element.

responsiveBehavior.fromDesktop: From 1024 px: the logo, the links, and the actions in one row; dropdown lists open below their buttons.
responsiveBehavior.belowDesktop: Below 1024 px: the logo, the Menu button, and the actions that fit; everything else is in the menu dialog.
responsiveBehavior.reflow: At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways, and labels wrap instead of being cut off.

variants.marketing: Links, dropdowns for groups of pages, and one call to action. A call to action that goes to a page is a link.
variants.app: Links, notifications, and the account menu (implementationDetails.appActions). The bar stays solid.
variants.transparent: Optional, for marketing pages: the bar starts transparent over a hero and turns solid once the page scrolls. An IntersectionObserver on a small element at the top of the page switches it exactly at the threshold, with no scroll listener; the same observer can add a shadow. The bar's text meets 4.5:1 against what's behind it in both states, the hero image included. App bars stay solid.

navItems.shape: { label, href?, current?, external?, unavailable?, items?: NavItem[] }
navItems.notes: An item with items is a dropdown; with an href as well, it gets both a link and a button. external links say they open a new tab; unavailable items follow componentSpec.anatomy.slotNotes.unavailableLink.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the lists and the menu appear without movement.

requirements.1.3.1: The bar is the header landmark, the links are in a labelled nav, and dropdown buttons expose their state.
requirements.1.4.1: The current page's link is marked by more than color.
requirements.1.4.3: Link text meets 4.5:1, over a transparent bar's background too.
requirements.1.4.11: Focus indicators and the current link's marker meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: Every link, dropdown, and the menu work from the keyboard.
requirements.2.4.1: A skip link goes past the bar to the main area.
requirements.2.4.3: Focus returns to the dropdown's button on Escape, and to the Menu button when the menu closes.
requirements.2.4.7: Every link and button shows focus.
requirements.2.4.11: scroll-padding-top keeps a focused element clear of the sticky bar.
requirements.2.5.8: Links and buttons are at least 24 px tall.
requirements.4.1.2: Dropdown buttons expose aria-expanded; the menu is a named dialog.

keyboardNavigation.tab: Moves through the skip link, the logo, the links and dropdown buttons, an open list's links, and the actions, in that order.
keyboardNavigation.enterSpace: Opens or closes a dropdown, and follows links.
keyboardNavigation.escape: Closes the open list or the menu, with focus back on its button.

unavailableLink.note: Only for a link that has to show as unavailable for now

notificationsBadge.note: The button's name has the count

screenReader.landmarks: The banner, and a navigation landmark named "Main"; the menu dialog has its own nav.
screenReader.dropdowns: Each dropdown button reads its name and "collapsed" or "expanded".

focusManagement.dropdowns: Focus stays on the button when the list opens, and Tab moves on into the list. One list is open at a time. A closed list has the hidden attribute, so its links aren't in the Tab order.
focusManagement.menu: The menu is a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), named "Main menu". The browser makes the rest of the page inert, closes it on Escape, and returns focus to the Menu button (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Without a native dialog, follow the Modal Dialog guide's model: the rest of the page inert, and no focus-trap library.
focusManagement.notObscured: scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to the bar's height, makes the page scroll focused elements and link targets clear of the bar (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11). Without it, a link focused under the bar stays covered (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Where the bar's height changes, as on phones, set the value again; keep the bar to one line so its height holds.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

disclosure.description: Disclosure dropdowns: a button that shows or hides its list of links, one list at a time, with Escape back to the button, and closing when focus leaves the navigation or on a click outside.
disclosure.html:

skipLink.description: The skip link as the header's first child, shown while it has focus, and the sticky bar with scroll-padding-top at its height.
skipLink.html: Skip to content Acme

implementationDetails.sticky: position: sticky with top: 0 keeps the bar at the top without a script. Switching to position: fixed from a scroll handler makes the content jump up by the bar's height. scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to the bar's height, makes the page scroll focused elements and link targets clear of the bar (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11). Without it, a link focused under the bar stays covered (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Where the bar's height changes, as on phones, set the value again; keep the bar to one line so its height holds.
implementationDetails.transparentState: Optional, for marketing pages: the bar starts transparent over a hero and turns solid once the page scrolls. An IntersectionObserver on a small element at the top of the page switches it exactly at the threshold, with no scroll listener; the same observer can add a shadow. The bar's text meets 4.5:1 against what's behind it in both states, the hero image included. App bars stay solid.
implementationDetails.mobileMenu: Below 1024 px, the links and the actions move into a menu opened by a Menu button. It's one switch: from 1024 px the bar shows its links, below that the Menu button. The menu is a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), named "Main menu". The browser makes the rest of the page inert, closes it on Escape, and returns focus to the Menu button (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Without a native dialog, follow the Modal Dialog guide's model: the rest of the page inert, and no focus-trap library. It has a visible Close button ("Close menu"), and it also closes on a click on the backdrop and when a link in it is followed. Inside it, an item with children is an accordion section: a button with aria-expanded that shows its links. Opening one doesn't close the menu, and several can be open. The page behind doesn't scroll: overflow: hidden on the root element while the menu is open (html:has(dialog:modal)), with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page doesn't shift. When the window crosses 1024 px, focus on an element that hides moves to the nearest control that stays, and focus anywhere else stays where it is. Widening with the menu open closes it and moves focus to the same link in the bar; widening with focus on the Menu button, which hides, moves focus to the current page's link in the bar. In both cases, when that link is in a closed dropdown list, focus goes to the first link in the bar that shows instead; narrowing with focus on the bar's links, which hide, moves focus to the Menu button. React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events. Chromium drops focus from an element a media query hides before the listener runs, so remember the last focused element and check whether it still shows. The menu's copy of the links gets its own ids.
implementationDetails.appActions: The account menu is a disclosure like the dropdowns: a button named "Account" (or the person's name) with aria-expanded, and a list of links. Sign out is a button that posts a form, not a link. The notifications button's name includes the count ("Notifications, 3 unread"), and the badge is hidden from screen readers, since the name already says it. The badge isn't a live region; new notifications, if announced at all, go through one polite status region.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The bar is a sticky bar: an open dropdown list sits above the page, and a modal dialog covers the bar.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. The bar is 72 px tall from 1024 px and 60 px below. Links are 16 px, and links and buttons are at least 24 px tall (44 px is comfortable for touch). Text meets 4.5:1, and focus indicators and the current link's marker 3:1. A badge with white text needs a dark enough red: #dc2626 is 4.8:1, #ef4444 only 3.8:1. Check the project's own colors the same way. Labels wrap; nothing is cut off with an ellipsis. At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways. Motion is optional: a list fades in over 150 ms, and the menu slides in over 250 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, they appear without movement.

edgeCases.manyLinks: Group them into dropdowns, or switch to the menu at a wider breakpoint, so the row never wraps under the bar.
edgeCases.noScript: Render the links on the server. A dropdown's parent can be a link to an overview page, so every page is reachable before the script runs.
edgeCases.routeChange: A route change closes an open list and the menu, and moves aria-current.
edgeCases.focusReturnTarget: If the button that opened something is gone when it closes, move focus somewhere sensible nearby, such as the bar's first link, never the page's body.

must: Build on the project's header or navigation component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Use disclosure buttons for dropdowns, and hide closed lists
Keep focused elements clear of the sticky bar with scroll-padding-top
Use a native dialog, or the Modal Dialog guide's model, for the menu below 1024 px
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a focus-trap or scroll-lock library, without asking
Use role="menu", role="menuitem", or aria-haspopup for lists of links
Switch the bar to position: fixed from a scroll handler
Handle Escape with a document-wide listener that stops other handlers
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The page starts with a "Skip to content" link that shows when it has focus and moves focus to the main area
The bar sticks to the top with CSS alone, and a link focused under it is scrolled clear of it (scroll-padding-top at the bar's height)
The bar is the page's header, its links are in a labelled nav, and the current page's link has aria-current="page"
Each dropdown is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls and no aria-haspopup, and a closed list is hidden
Focus stays on the button when its list opens, Tab moves through the list's links, and one list is open at a time
Escape closes the open list and returns focus to its button; a click outside, or focus leaving the navigation, closes it too
Lists open on a click, Enter, or Space, never on hover alone
Below 1024 px, a Menu button opens the links in a native dialog named "Main menu", with a visible Close button
While the menu is open, the rest of the page is inert and doesn't scroll; Close, Escape, the backdrop, and a followed link close it, and focus returns to the Menu button

Crossing 1024 px either way, focus on what hides moves to what stays: from the menu or the Menu button to the bar's links when widening, and from the bar's links to the Menu button when narrowing; focus anywhere else stays where it is
The account menu is a disclosure with a Sign out button, and the notifications button's name includes the unread count
An open modal dialog covers the bar, and a transparent bar's text meets 4.5:1 over whatever is behind it
Labels wrap instead of being cut off, nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide, and under reduced motion nothing slides
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens

Optional: an app shell whose header has the same account menu and notifications.
